correctness.rationale: The patch replaces the two hard-coded install.sh/test.sh checks with an explicit array covering all five requested glob patterns (*.sh, scripts/*.sh, scripts/checks/*.sh, scripts/setup/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh), enables nullglob during expansion, and loops with bash -n plus independent pass()/fail() per file—matching the parser-only, explicit-glob, per-file reporting contract. One-point deduction for redirecting bash -n stderr to /dev/null (hides failure diagnostics) and because bundle evidence cannot confirm whether expanded coverage revealed latent syntax errors elsewhere requiring fixes in the same diff.

quality.rationale: Implementation is minimal, readable, and repo-consistent: nullglob with an explicit glob list and a straightforward two-loop expansion over pass()/fail() helpers, scoped to the single required check file. Deductions for stderr suppression on bash -n failures, absence of inline comments documenting glob rationale or empty-set handling, no defensive file-existence guard before bash -n, and overlapping patterns may re-check the same script multiple times without deduplication.

process.rationale: Diff is tightly focused on scripts/checks/055-script-syntax.sh with no unrelated churn (objective scope penalties fully satisfied at 15/15). Bundle contains no verification notes, bash test.sh output, narrow syntax-check output, negative-smoke demonstration/explanation, or documented no-change doc-sync decision required by acceptance criteria, so full plan/verification discipline cannot be confirmed from bundle evidence alone.

reliability.rationale: Objective evidence confirms test wiring (6/6) and bash_n_check_script pass, and the diff integrates with existing pass/fail helpers. Bundle lacks full_test_sh execution evidence (skipped in bundle-only grading), no reported command output, and no negative-smoke test or explanation that a deliberate syntax error is caught and cleared, leaving verification discipline thin despite plausible wiring.

uncertainty_notes: Bundle contains no bash test.sh run output, narrow syntax-check output, or negative-smoke demonstration/explanation required by acceptance criteria; reliability scored conservatively.
